title: Fields of definition of dynamical systems on $ mathbb{P}^{1}$. Improvements on a result of Silverman

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: In the converse direction of the proof, the text states: 'if σ ∈ Gal(K/k_ξ), then there exists f ∈ PGL₂(K) such that φ^σ = f∘φ∘f⁻¹. Since φ^σ = τ_σ∘φ∘τ_σ⁻¹, this implies that τ_σ∘f⁻¹ is an element of N_φ mapping to σ.' A direct check shows that h' = τ_σ∘f⁻¹ does not in general satisfy h'φh'⁻¹ = φ (the defining property of N_φ): expanding h'φh'⁻¹ = τ_σ f⁻¹ φ f τ_σ⁻¹ = τ_σ (f⁻¹φf) τ_σ⁻¹, which equals φ only if f⁻¹φf = τ_σ⁻¹φτ_σ, a relation not implied by the hypothesis fφf⁻¹ = τ_σφτ_σ⁻¹. Instead, substituting from the hypothesis shows that h = f⁻¹∘τ_σ (not τ_σ∘f⁻¹) satisfies hφh⁻¹ = φ: f⁻¹τ_σφτ_σ⁻¹f = f⁻¹(fφf⁻¹)f = φ. This is consistent with the forward direction of the same proof, which correctly uses g = τ_σ∘f⁻¹ as the *conjugator* taking φ to φ^σ (a different role than the converse direction requires, namely an element that *commutes* with φ). The composition order in the converse-direction construction thus appears to be incorrect, making the stated element not actually an element of N_φ in general.

The proof states: 'The assumption is equivalent to saying that |S(K)| is odd; if char k ≠ 2, this is equivalent to saying that S has odd degree. We conclude that P(k_ξ) ≠ ∅ by [Bre24, Lemma 27].' This argument is only carried out under the assumption char k ≠ 2, with no parallel argument given for char k = 2, leaving an apparent gap in the proof of Theorem 12 for fields of characteristic 2 under this condition, in contrast to the analogous argument in Section 1 (for perfect fields) which is stated without any characteristic restriction.
